interpretation: The unconditional v6 asymmetry is explained by expansion direction: restrictive additions protected every baseline robust-impossible certificate, whereas permissive additions protected every baseline robust-reachable certificate.
The opposite certificate class was genuinely vulnerable: restrictive worlds erased 81 robust-reachability certificates and permissive worlds erased 1,445 robust-impossibility certificates.
The frozen candidate expansion was strongly skewed toward permissive worlds, with 1,583 permissive versus 151 restrictive additions, explaining why impossibility looked much less persistent in v6.
Incomparable worlds and newly admitted source hypotheses added further fragility but were secondary to the directional effect.
Reverse-impossibility reasoning is therefore robust only relative to a declared uncertainty family whose future additions are guaranteed not to be more permissive than the certified worlds.
claim_boundary: Restrictive/permissive are reachable-set inclusion classes, not claims of ecological plausibility.
The exact E1/E2 protections assume the source set is fixed to baseline-surviving sources.
Allowing new source hypotheses can add both kinds of fragility.
The result gives a condition for certificate persistence, not a universal priority for impossibility over possibility.
